a7030d0b5c9fd40d.description: Job description POSITION SUMMARY Our jobs aren’t just about putting food on the table that our guests will enjoy until they ask for their bill. Instead, we want to build an experience that is memorable and unique – with food and drinks on the side. Our Guest Service Experts take the initiative and deliver a wide range of services to make sure that guests enjoy their meal. Whether setting tables, communicating with the kitchen, interacting and serving guests, or cleaning work areas and supplies, the Guest Service Expert makes transactions feel like part of the experience. No matter what position you are in, there are a few things that are critical to success – creating a safe workplace, following company policies and procedures, upholding quality standards, and ensuring your uniform, personal appearance, and communications are professional. Guest Service Experts will be on their feet and moving around (stand, sit, or walk for an extended time; moving over sloping, uneven, or slippery surfaces), managing the menu (read and visually verify information), and taking a hands-on approach to work (move, lift, carry, push, pull, and place objects weighing less than or equal to 25 pounds without assistance and 50 pounds with assistance; reach overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping). Doing all these things well (and other reasonable job duties as requested) is critical for Guest Service Experts – to get it right for our guests and our business each and every time. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Education: High school diploma or G.E.D. equivalent. Related Work Experience: Less than 1 year related work experience. Supervisory Experience: No supervisory experience. License or Certification: None At Marriott International, we are dedicated to being an equal opportunity employer, welcoming all and providing access to opportunity. We actively foster an environment where the unique backgrounds of our associates are valued and celebrated. Our greatest strength lies in the rich blend of culture, talent, and experiences of our associates. We are committed to non-discrimination on any protected basis, including disability, veteran status, or other basis protected by applicable law. EDITION Hotels combine the visionary genius of boutique hotelier Ian Schrager, the service delivery of a world-class luxury hotel, and the global reach of Marriott International to create an entirely new experience in the world of hospitality. EDITION delivers the best of both worlds in a delicate balancing act – polish with personality, perfectionism with individualism, and comfort with charisma and charm. The brand targets sophisticated, knowledgeable consumers who understand quality, originality, design, and service excellence, but who want it without limitations – breaking the bounds of convention and demanding an attitude and a feeling wrapped in a package that showcases the exceptional. But to create this magical experience, we need you. We are looking for outgoing, authentically amazing people who are looking for a place to work that inspires them, challenges them and makes them proud to come to work. A place where service comes from the heart, not from a handbook. A place that delivers a never-ending theatrical performance that continuously delights and enchants each and every one of our guests. We invite you to join us today. In joining EDITION, you join a portfolio of brands with Marriott International. Be where you can do your best work,​ begin your purpose, belong to an amazing global​ team, and become the best version of you. Preferred candidate Years of experience 1+ years Degree Bachelor's degree / higher diploma

a70461ebb3d1fe2a.job_title: Associate Director-Advisory & Risk Consulting | Risk & Resilience
a70461ebb3d1fe2a.description: The opportunity Control Risks is strengthening its Advisory & Risk Consulting presence in Saudi Arabia. We are seeking a senior consulting leader who can combine high-quality client delivery with business development, key account leadership and practice building. Based permanently in Riyadh, the Associate Director will be the in-country senior lead for our risk and resilience consulting work and an important bridge between Saudi clients, the Middle East and EMEA team and our wider global network. This is a hands-on leadership role. The successful candidate will lead complex engagements, develop trusted senior client relationships, convert opportunities into sustainable mandates and help build a scalable and highly profitable Saudi practice. The role will initially focus on organisational resilience, including enterprise risk management, security management, business continuity and crisis management, while connecting clients to the wider capabilities of Control Risks where relevant. Success in this role means: excellent delivery on current mandates, strong direct client relationships, a growing and well-managed Saudi business pipeline, and a capable in-country team that can scale with demand. Role purpose To lead the origination, sale and delivery of Advisory & Risk Consulting engagements in Saudi Arabia, with primary responsibility for enterprise risk management, business continuity, crisis management and organisational resilience. The Associate Director will own key client relationships and opportunities end-to-end, ensure engagements are commercially and technically successful, develop junior colleagues and help establish Control Risks as the specialist risk and resilience adviser of choice in the Kingdom. Client delivery and technical leadership Lead complex consulting engagements from scoping and mobilisation through delivery, quality assurance, closure and follow-on work. Act as engagement lead and senior client adviser across organisational resilience, including enterprise risk management, , security management, business continuity, crisis management and emergency preparedness. Translate recognised standards and good practice into pragmatic, locally relevant solutions that work in the client’s operating environment. Facilitate executive interviews, workshops, simulations and decision-making sessions with boards, C-suite leaders and senior management. Maintain strong control of scope, quality, resourcing, budget, schedule, risk and client expectations. Remain actively involved in delivery, providing visible senior leadership while enabling consultants to take meaningful responsibility. Business development and account growth Lead business development for Advisory & Risk Consulting in Saudi Arabia, working in strong collaboration with the Middle East practice leader and in close partnership with in-country colleagues and other business lines. Build trusted relationships with senior decision-makers and position Control Risks around the client’s strategic, operational and regulatory priorities. Own opportunities end-to-end: qualification, solution design, teaming, proposal development, pricing, negotiation, conversion and transition into delivery. Develop and execute focused account plans for priority Saudi clients and identify opportunities for repeat, programme-based and multidisciplinary work. Maintain accurate and timely pipeline, forecast and client activity information, and contribute to disciplined commercial decision-making. Represent Control Risks in relevant client events, roundtables and thought-leadership activities in the Kingdom. Practice building and people leadership Help establish a sustainable in-country delivery model and contribute to the growth of the Saudi Advisory & Risk Consulting team. Coach, mentor and provide real-time feedback to consultants, strengthening technical capability, consulting skills and commercial judgement. Plan resource requirements across the Saudi portfolio and draw effectively on regional and global expertise when specialist support is required. Capture and protect Control Risks intellectual property, embed lessons learned and improve the reuse of methods, tools and high-quality deliverables. Contribute to recruitment, onboarding, performance management and succession planning as the practice grows. Promote a collaborative “one firm” culture across Saudi Arabia, the wider Middle East and global teams. Work under the direction of the EMEA Head and the Middle East Leader of Advisory & Risk Consulting, while actively contributing to the EMEA and global Advisory & Risk Consulting teams. Innovation, technology and risk management Advance the responsible use of data, automation and emerging technology in our consulting propositions, methods and delivery toolkits. Identify opportunities to connect risk and resilience work with cyber, technology, intelligence, security and other Control Risks capabilities. Ensure engagements comply with applicable legal, risk, contracting, information-management and professional standards. Model sound commercial judgement, professional integrity and disciplined management of sensitive client information. Essential experience A strong track record in a consulting environment, with substantial experience, typically 8-10 years’, leading enterprise risk, security management, business continuity, crisis management or organisational resilience engagements. Demonstrated experience leading multiple complex client engagements and being accountable for delivery quality and commercial outcomes. Proven ability to originate work, grow accounts and convert opportunities through trusted senior relationships and compelling proposals. Credibility with executive and senior management stakeholders, including the confidence to challenge constructively and influence decisions. GCC experience and a strong understanding of how to deliver consulting work in Saudi Arabia; prior experience working with Saudi clients is essential. Experience managing, coaching and developing consultants in a high-performance, collaborative environment. Excellent written and spoken English, with the ability to produce concise, high-quality executive materials. Willingness and ability to be based permanently in Riyadh and travel within the Kingdom and wider region as required. Preferred experience Saudi nationals are strongly encouraged to apply. Preference may be given to suitably qualified Saudi nationals in line with applicable localisation requirements and hiring laws. Fluent Arabic speaking and writing. Experience in one or more priority sectors such as government, sovereign and Vision 2030 entities, technology, entertainment, financial services, energy, critical infrastructure, industrials or logistics. Experience delivering multidisciplinary programmes that integrate risk, resilience, technology, intelligence or security expertise. Experience building a consulting capability, proposition or team in a growth market. Familiarity with technology-enabled risk and resilience solutions, analytics and responsible uses of AI. Qualifications and professional standing Relevant bachelor’s degree or equivalent professional experience. Recognised professional qualifications in risk, security management, business continuity, crisis management or a related field, such as IRM, MBCI/CBCI, CBCP or equivalent. A relevant master’s degree or postgraduate qualification is advantageous. Capabilities and behaviours Commercial and business intellect Client-centric judgement Executive presence and personal impact Structured problem-solving Clear, persuasive communication Ownership and accountability Inclusive people leadership Collaboration across disciplines and geographies Adaptability and tenacity Integrity, discretion and professionalism Control Risks offers a competitively positioned compensation and benefits package that is transparent and summarised in the full job offer. Private medical insurance Annual Housing Allowance Compulsory

Job Description The Accountant is responsible for supporting the day-to-day accounting operations of the company by maintaining accurate financial records, ensuring transactions are properly recorded, and assisting with reconciliations and financial reporting. The role covers a broad range of accounting activities, including transaction recording, inventory accounting, sales reconciliation, payroll review, VAT compliance, and financial documentation while ensuring adherence to company policies, accounting standards, and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Key Responsibilities Accounting Records Record daily financial transactions in the accounting system. Prepare and post journal entries with proper supporting documentation. Maintain accurate and organized financial records. Accounts Processing Record supplier invoices and assist with supplier payment processing in coordination with the Finance Manager. Record customer payments and monitor receivable balances. Ensure expenses are recorded accurately and allocated to the appropriate accounts. Store & POS Reconciliation Reconcile store sales with POS reports and system records. Review store cash deposits and investigate discrepancies. Ensure accurate recording of sales from all channels, including retail stores and online platforms. Inventory Accounting Record inventory transactions and adjustments in the accounting system. Assist in reconciling physical inventory with system records. Support stock count procedures and investigate inventory variances. Calculate and allocate landed costs (freight, customs duties, and related import expenses) to inventory to ensure accurate product costing. Bank & Account Reconciliation Perform regular bank reconciliations and investigate discrepancies. Reconcile supplier, customer, and other balance sheet accounts. Review account balances to ensure accuracy and completeness. Financial Closing Assist with monthly financial closing activities. Ensure transactions are recorded in the correct accounting period. Payroll & Employee Earnings Review Review employee payroll records, including salaries, allowances, overtime, and other earnings before processing. Ensure payroll calculations are accurate and supported by approved documentation. Verify that payroll entries are correctly recorded in the accounting system and allocated to the appropriate accounts. VAT Compliance Ensure transactions are properly recorded for VAT purposes. Expense Review & Control Review expense claims and supporting documents for completeness and compliance with company policies. Ensure expenses are properly authorized before recording them. a7240bed48fd3a40.description: About the Role The Islamic Development Bank is seeking a Senior Climate Change Specialist to join its team in Jeddah. This contract position requires 5-10 years of experience and focuses on providing senior-level technical and professional expertise to advance the Bank's climate action, green growth, and sustainability agenda across various initiatives, including mitigation, adaptation, resilience, and nature-based solutions. The specialist will support the Bank in enhancing the development impact of its operations. Job Purpose The Senior Climate Change Specialist will participate as a core team member in the identification, preparation, appraisal, and implementation support of projects and programs. This includes climate risk screening, GHG accounting, climate finance qualification, and Paris alignment assessment. The role also involves supporting the mainstreaming of climate and environmental considerations within the Bank’s systems, policies, and standards, such as the Environmental and Social Framework and sustainable finance architecture. The specialist will assist Member Countries in implementing their Nationally Determined Contributions, National Adaptation Plans, long-term low-emission development strategies, and net-zero pathways. Key Responsibilities Contribute to the development of strategic plans, analytics, and guidance related to climate mitigation, adaptation, and environmental sustainability. Lead input on climate change aspects during project identification, appraisal, design, processing, and approval, including physical and transition climate risk screening, GHG accounting, and climate co-benefit qualification. Support the Bank’s alignment with the Paris Agreement and the consistent application of agreed assessment methods by project teams. Support the interface between the climate agenda and the Bank’s Environmental and Social Standards, including climate-related aspects of risk screening, resource efficiency, and nature-based solutions. Co-lead Communities of Practice in selected sectors on climate mitigation and adaptation, providing technical leadership and participating in MDB Working Groups. Contribute to the delivery of global engagement products on climate mitigation and adaptation, and participate in country dialogues and capacity building workshops in Member Countries. Support the achievement of the Bank’s corporate climate finance target, including adaptation finance ambition, and track commitments and progress. Apply joint MDB methodologies for tracking climate change mitigation and adaptation finance, ensuring consistent classification. Support the operationalization and management of the Physical Climate Risk Management System and ensure implementation of best practices in climate adaptation and resilience measures. Contribute to articulating the Bank’s Islamic finance offer for climate action, including blended and Shari’ah-compliant instruments. Identify, assess, and monitor capacity development needs for internal and external stakeholders, designing and administering relevant interventions. Contribute to the Division’s engagement with international climate finance institutions and coordinate fundraising for relevant IsDB climate-tagged projects. Prepare and quality-assure concept notes, funding proposals, and terms of reference for submission to climate funds. Collaborate with academia, MDBs, UN agencies, and other partners on research, analysis, and outreach, supporting the Bank’s engagement with UNFCCC, UNCBD, and UNCCD processes. Track external issues and best practices in climate mitigation and adaptation, providing technical support to Management on engagement in key external processes. Contribute to knowledge products, guidance notes, policy briefs, and case studies capturing lessons from the Bank’s climate portfolio. Contribute to the preparation of progress reports on project cycle activities and ensure climate-relevant core results indicators are included at the design stage. Contribute to divisional and departmental results and KPI reporting, and to the evidence base supporting Management and Board reporting on the climate portfolio. Contribute to the Bank’s external climate reporting commitments, including joint MDB climate finance reporting. Experience and Qualifications Candidates should possess 8-10 years of relevant experience in climate change and environmental sustainability. The role requires a strong technical and professional background in climate mitigation, adaptation, and resilience, with practical experience in project identification, appraisal, and implementation support. Familiarity with climate risk screening, GHG accounting, climate finance qualification, and Paris Agreement alignment is essential. Experience in resource mobilization and partnership building with international climate finance institutions is also required. Work Environment This role is based in Jeddah and operates on a contract basis. The specialist will work within the Climate Change and Environment Division, collaborating with other Global Practices and Regional Hubs in the Operations Complex. The position involves coordinating the work of consultants and less experienced team members. Application Process Further details on the application process will be provided upon inquiry. The salary for this position is not disclosed.

أعلاه إلى تقديم طلباتهم.
